translated_text: Haci lady! + I wish you all the best for your trip. Thank you so much for everything. Unfortunately, the various authors didn't want us to see each other before your departure. Nevertheless, I will try to do fruitful work for you. 7. Uler evening. Yours, Bob. And Solben, I received the approval for the plane ticket. rs I have Peats, haugh & Art, depending on whether I have Peatz. So I'll definitely come to Pemptens. Yours, Bob. p. 1.38 Zabūs, your letter finally arrived last night. However, I can't understand why you couldn't get any mail for 10 days. Besides, I always wrote immediately when I knew something definite. = Little one, I won't complain anymore, but if this goes on for days, I'm ready for a sanatorium. It's a shame that so much valuable energy is wasted. The 3-day journey didn't bother me at all. I still need three visas: Hungary, Yugoslavia, and Switzerland. The Yugoslavian one was rejected yesterday, so I have to submit it in Belgrade, and that takes days. In my desperation, I called the Foreign Ministry again. Dr. From called today and I was told he'd come back. I went there immediately, spoke with his representative, we had another phone consultation, and now I'm sitting downstairs in the Finance Ministry waiting for the letter they'll give me for the National Bank. So I'm making one more attempt to get the plane ticket approved! Zabūs, you'll only be able to understand all of this when I tell you everything in person. It couldn't be more complicated. What you know is at most 10% of it. I'm handling it all personally. It's nerve-wracking. Do you know how happy I'd be if I could just put all this behind me?! You can be sure I'm doing everything I can. Sure, I've made mistakes, but if you knew everything beforehand... Regarding Troc's letter, the telegram I sent regarding my visit today has of course become irrelevant due to the letter. Little one, please don't be impatient; I'm already impatient enough. His Zob.
